reviews.title: I want to like it except that it’s not enjoyable.
reviews.text:
Besides the micro fees being a bit laughable, peacock posturing and all, I thought I could ignore it while I explore whether this app is worth playing long term. It’s not. 

I gave this app two attempts; the first time I wasn’t impressed by the simplicity of the character customization, but I think it works for the user interface. I didn’t seek this out because I was getting something out of its aesthetic. I forgot about it and picked it back up. Then the second experience reminded me why I put this down in the first place- it’s not visually appealing, the micro fees are a cash grab in the dark, and you can’t go more than five exploratory taps before an unprompted AD takes over your screen. 

I can’t even play your game- without paying, and I wouldn’t even want to beyond this experience. You don’t have to waste your time here, dear user; you can move on.

reviews.title: Great game
reviews.text: This game is fantastic and ticks a lot of boxes other miss. However the business side of them game can be huge with the right updates. I spend 90% of my time dealing with them rather than doing other things. Setting up a way to have resource flow paths would be a huge time saver and a way to make the businesses a little more passive income. Also expanding on the housing market would be another amazing upgrade. Make duplex quadplex etc. More businesses would also take this game to a whole new level like restaurants that require farms to grow food. This is an amazing game I would recommend to anyone that has an itch for a good life sim game

reviews.title: detail is top tier
reviews.text:
Man, the few things i do have to gripe about are how tedious some things are. I feel like at a certain point businesses should have a manager that sells and sends product to next business.
Talents are so hard to build. I can only assume you would have to build while youre young. They have a cooldown of days, so its hard to keep track of. 

Yes days, not months or year based. That is one thing I like about the game. Its time scale runs as like 10 seconds = 1 day. You can pause the time to micromanage specifics, but some options are locked, such as spending time with a person. You can only action with that person once a day, but several others in a single day. This becomes a problem though, as like I said with the businesses, you would have to individually go through and choose the best option for that person. It becomes tedious after awhile.

I loved the house  and market design. 
A store design in the same fashion could be cool to see. Wish work had opportunities for advancement than just amount of days worked in previous position.
Bitcoin and a few other trophy items prices should be constantly changing imo too.

reviews.title: Great Game However…
reviews.text:
I would just like to say the game is actually decently made and in some aspects, great! There are some minor problems such as advertisements. I cannot explain how much money they made off of me just by setting my phone down. On average I would say I get an ad every minute and a half. It is ridiculous, not to mention annoying. The weird part is every time I stop to think about my next move or lay my phone down for a few seconds (at least 3 seconds) an ad starts to play. It makes me want to cringe. 
The next topic I have a hard time getting around is the fact that after your child turns 13 you won’t be able to spend time with them regularly to increase the relationship. I am unsure if this only lasts for the age of 13 but the only way I can increase my relationship with them is to give them money. It is absolute cringe. 
Please excuse my grammar as my auto-correct gets out of hand sometimes. That’s all I have to say.
